details:
MissionCraft — Spacecraft Engineering & Exploration Simulator

MissionCraft is a spacecraft engineering and space exploration simulation game developed in 48 hours for the NASA Space Apps Challenge 2026.

What Does It Do?

Built using C++17 and SDL3, MissionCraft allows players to design modular spacecraft, manage resources, select launch vehicles, and plan missions to different destinations.

Players can experiment with spacecraft components, monitor mass, fuel capacity, and power requirements, and choose between four launch vehicles: SSLV, PSLV, GSLV, and Falcon 9. The game also includes spacecraft configurations, launch vehicle compatibility checks, mission planning, mission control, and save/load functionality.

Benefits and Intended Impact

MissionCraft makes aerospace engineering concepts more accessible through interactive gameplay. It introduces players to spacecraft design, resource management, payload limitations, and mission planning while encouraging curiosity about space exploration and STEM fields.

Technologies Used

  • C++17: Core programming and game logic.
  • SDL3: Rendering, window management, and input handling.
  • SDL3_image, SDL3_ttf, SDL3_mixer: Images, fonts, and audio.
  • nlohmann/json: Configuration and save/load management.
  • GNU Make, GCC, MSYS2: Build environment and automation.
  • GitHub: Version control and collaboration.

Creativity and Development Considerations

MissionCraft combines spacecraft engineering concepts with interactive simulation mechanics. Players experience how component selection, spacecraft mass, fuel requirements, and launch vehicle limitations influence mission readiness.

Given the 48-hour development timeframe, our team prioritized modular architecture, functional gameplay, intuitive interfaces, engineering constraints, and future scalability.

Future Vision

We aim to expand MissionCraft with more advanced aerospace mechanics, including delta-v calculations, orbital transfers, fuel consumption, and spacecraft staging.

MissionCraft — Design. Engineer. Explore.
